title: Ringed slice equivalences and module restriction squares
statement: Let e:(Sh(C),R)→(Sh(D),S) be a ringed-topos equivalence with invertible structural map, for small sites and commutative coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Choose element-site slice adjunction data [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] on both sides. For every sheaf A on D there is a ringed equivalence s_A from the element site of e.inverse(A) with R to the element site of A with S. Its inverse image is the conjugate, by the given fibre equivalences, of Over.post(e.inverse). There is a natural isomorphism e.inverse⋙j_eA*≅j_A*⋙s_A.inverse satisfying the restricted structural-map equation. For every whole and slice module-equivalence package tied to e and s_A as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-comparison-data], these module equivalences commute with restriction to A and with further restriction along every B→A.

source.place: Tags 04IE and 04J4, applied to an equivalence

proof.text: Apply e.inverse to objects and arrows over A. The inverse on over-categories applies e.direct and uses the invertible adjunction unit to identify e.direct(e.inverse(A)) with A. The original unit and counit give the slice equivalence. Conjugate with the given element-site fibre equivalences. Finite-product comparisons identify the restricted ring, and the image of e.ringMap is the invertible structural map. The fibre comparison gives q and its displayed structural identity.

Construct the induced module direct images from these geometric ring data. Both routes around a module restriction square have the same set-sheaf functor and scalar action, by the structural identity. The fibre comparison and its inverse are therefore linear and natural. For B→A the same argument uses the fibre product over A and gives the further-restriction square.

The module functor in any supplied presentation package has inverse naturally isomorphic to the induced module direct image. Uniqueness of left adjoints transports the constructed module comparisons to those supplied functors. This proves the quantified assertion for all whole and slice packages and every continuous further restriction.

theorem ringed_equivalence_slices
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} {S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u}}
    (e : RingedToposMorphism (localCoefficientRings R) (localCoefficientRings S))
    [e.inverse.IsEquivalence] [IsIso e.ringMap]
    (sourceSlices : ∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u),
      RingedSheafSliceAdjunctionData (localCoefficientRings S) A)
    (targetSlices : ∀ A : Sheaf J (Type u),
      RingedSheafSliceAdjunctionData (localCoefficientRings R) A) :
    ∃ (s : ∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u),
        RingedToposMorphism
          (localCoefficientRings (presentationElementRing R (e.inverse.obj A)))
          (localCoefficientRings (presentationElementRing S A)))
      (h : ∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u), (s A).inverse.IsEquivalence)
      (k : ∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u), IsIso (s A).ringMap)
      (q : ∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u),
        e.inverse ⋙ elementSheafPullback (e.inverse.obj A) ≅
          elementSheafPullback A ⋙ (s A).inverse),
      (∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u), Nonempty ((s A).inverse ≅
        (sourceSlices A).fibreEquivalence.functor ⋙ Over.post e.inverse ⋙
          (targetSlices (e.inverse.obj A)).fibreEquivalence.inverse)) ∧
      (∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u),
        (q A).hom.app ((sheafCompose K (forget RingCat)).obj (localCoefficientRings S)) ≫
          (s A).ringMap = (elementSheafPullback (e.inverse.obj A)).map e.ringMap) ∧
      ∀ (whole : RingedPresentationAt e)
        (T : ∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u), RingedPresentationAt (s A))
        (rs : RingedPresentationRestrictions S) (rt : RingedPresentationRestrictions R),
        (∀ A : Sheaf K (Type u),
          Nonempty (whole.transport.modules.functor ⋙
            elementModulePullback.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings R) (e.inverse.obj A) ≅
              elementModulePullback.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings S) A ⋙
                (T A).transport.modules.functor)) ∧
        ∀ {A B : Sheaf K (Type u)} (b : B ⟶ A),
          Nonempty ((T A).transport.modules.functor ⋙
            elementModulePullbackOver.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings R) (e.inverse.map b)
              (rt.overContinuous (e.inverse.map b)) ≅
            elementModulePullbackOver.{u, u} (localCoefficientRings S) b
              (rs.overContinuous b) ⋙ (T B).transport.modules.functor)
